intended_object: An index type used in the proof: the variables not in S, together with the variables of S other than a chosen pivot i, which stand for the ratios X_j/X_i. It is used to build a coefficient field for the weight-one valuation construction (inferred from the docstring and from its uses in the same file).
explanation: The definition is only a sum type `{j // j ∉ S} ⊕ {j // j ∈ S ∧ j ≠ i}`. The file uses it to index the variables of an auxiliary polynomial ring. That ring, and its fraction field, come from the change of variables σ ≃ Option (WeightOneCoefficientVariables S i): the pivot variable becomes `none` and the other variables of S become the ratios to the pivot. It is bookkeeping for one proof. The literature has no standard object that it formalizes. As an indexing device it does what its docstring says.
